rationale.usefulness: The tagged Apps, Agent and datasette-llm releases support concrete improvements for database-backed teaching labs and collection websites: linked record views, a homepage entry point and directly configured local endpoints. The report supplies checkable answer keys, forbidden-record and missing-value tests, accessibility checks and a narrated SQL demonstration. It also gives useful deployment guidance about credentials, grants, partial write completion and patch scope. Actual model/server compatibility remains untested.
rationale.impact: These are useful incremental improvements to an existing Datasette ecosystem rather than a substantial advance in AI methods or broadly demonstrated agent capability. Local endpoint configuration and linked app state lower integration friction; the permission corrections are operationally important for affected users but do not establish field-wide significance. I assign impact 4 independently of length. The supplied 993-word count fits the 900–1,100 band for that impact; the coordinator must still apply the final two-review mean.
rationale.novelty: Fragment manifests, app_links and hash-aware debugging make the established database-to-app workflow more coherent, and direct OpenAI-compatible endpoint dictionaries reduce setup work. The underlying ideas of linked views, model adapters, human write approval and access controls are established. The report accurately treats earlier panel/grant features as context and does not claim a new general-purpose app-generation capability.
rationale.maturity: Tagged prereleases and clear documentation support a bounded pilot, not a dependable production guarantee. Saved primary pages confirm Stop lets an in-flight tool finish, earlier successful write statements are not rolled back, and the managed HTML sandbox does not encompass Python plugin apps. I checked the advisory affected range 1.0a31–1.0a42, patch 1.0a43, metadata/SQL-only disclosure scope, stable-branch exemption, and the distinct route/name download issue fixed in 0.65.6. The report preserves these boundaries and acknowledges main-branch documentation drift, without claiming runtime or security verification.
rationale.openness: The inspected Agent and Apps LICENSE captures show Apache 2.0, and the public release/README material describes inspectable SQL, stored app source, permissions and model endpoint configuration. Direct local endpoints strengthen portability without requiring a provider key in every setup. This is strong practical openness, but model/provider and dataset terms remain separate and no full reproducible deployment or arbitrary local-model compatibility has been demonstrated.
